title: Use SAGE-owned context for LLM role-agent handoffs while preserving Architect-LLM intent collaboration
failure_signature: A long-lived LLM conversation implicitly carries state across multiple SAGE responsibilities, allowing unaccepted model interpretations and task-level discoveries to become cross-role context and displace the Architect-owned objective or authoritative evidence.
symptoms: Small functional changes expand into many process or platform iterations.
Architect repeatedly restores objective focus or asks for functional progress.
Task-level defects become active work without deterministic objective impact.
Prior LLM narrative gains authority through conversational persistence.
Existing successful SAGE/Kalaxy3 evidence is underused or reinterpreted.
More iterations produce little externally exposable objective value.
root_cause: The working hypothesis is that conversational continuity is being used as an implicit shared-state mechanism for multiple LLM-delivered SAGE roles instead of SAGE explicitly constructing role-relevant authoritative context and governed handoffs.
known_resolution: Preserve the persistent Architect-LLM relationship at the intent layer.
Have SAGE assemble role-specific authoritative context for specialized LLM invocations.
Do not automatically propagate unaccepted LLM narrative between role-agents.
Use governed outputs and handoffs as cross-role state.
Test complete conversation wipe and role reconstruction from SAGE state.
Adopt graph-based role routing only if experiment evidence demonstrates need.
preventive_control: Do not treat conversation history alone as authoritative cross-agent state.
Preserve source/provenance distinctions in role context.
Require objective-level relevance before task defects alter active work.
Do not invalidate accepted historical success or current WIP solely because a new architecture is proposed.
preflight_detection: Compare fresh role-agent runs with accumulated-context and contaminated-context controls.
Measure Architect interventions needed to restore objective or context.
Verify a downstream role can continue after complete LLM-context loss using SAGE state only.
Verify prior successful evidence remains recognized and useful current capability is reused where applicable.
